# Test Utils against Hono's own HTTP observations

Run `deno test --no-check -A tests/hono-contracts.test.ts` from the repository root. The suite registers one test for
each authored vector and checks both candidates against literal expectations. It also checks vector identities and
provenance. It does not construct expected output by asking either candidate for its result.

The inputs and selected assertions are adapted from Hono **4.13.5**, commit
[`06880c4a2b04de9dd74217f26dd831209b9c01f1`](https://github.com/honojs/hono/tree/06880c4a2b04de9dd74217f26dd831209b9c01f1).
The upstream MIT notice is retained in [HONO-LICENSE](./HONO-LICENSE). Each vector records the upstream path, test
registration line and title in its source data. [coverage.json](./coverage.json) maps those vectors to the executable
suite; [the source inventory](../../../docs/hono-coverage.md) reports remaining unmapped registrations instead of
counting preserved upstream files as executed tests.

| Corpus                               | Vectors | What the assertions observe                                                  |
| ------------------------------------ | ------: | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [routes.ts](./routes.ts)             |     109 | Raw router matches, handler order, parameters, misses and rejected authoring |
| [requests.ts](./requests.ts)         |      28 | Query/header lookup, body views, forms/files and cloning ownership           |
| [responses.ts](./responses.ts)       |      44 | Body serialization, status, redirect locations and header/cookie output      |
| [applications.ts](./applications.ts) |      55 | Fetch routing, middleware, error mapping, mounts, strict slashes and HEAD    |

The common router suite uses Hono's `TrieRouter`, which runs that upstream common suite without skips. The application
suite uses Hono's standard `Hono` class. [hono.ts](./hono.ts) imports no production Utils packages;
[utils.ts](./utils.ts) imports Utils directly and does not use Hono or the Utils Hono adapter. The only shared
operations build observations from native responses and describe inputs. Each candidate creates its own requests, route
owners and middleware.

These rows qualify **selected observable assertions**, not every assertion in an upstream registration. For example, a
response assembly row can cover its status, body and initial header precedence while leaving later context mutations
unmapped. Header-only rows still consume their responses. Body-cache rows await each read; they do not preserve upstream
assertions that only check whether constructing an async function throws. Multipart boundaries are generated by the
native platform, so the suite compares field values and File contents instead of boundary strings.

The distinction between shared output and an API adaptation matters:

- Utils selects one route owner by specificity. Hono can collect multiple handlers in registration order. The raw router
  vectors execute and assert both outcomes, including duplicate ownership that Utils rejects.
- Hono supports wildcard, optional and regular-expression route grammar. Utils supports literal segments and named
  parameters. Rejected or literal-star Utils outcomes remain in the corpus; they are not rewritten into passing Hono
  grammar.
- Hono decodes literal path characters before matching. Utils matches the raw pathname. Encoded static and non-ASCII
  mount-prefix cases expose that difference.
- Hono automatically caches body views and can reconstruct a consumed request. The Utils cache examples explicitly
  compose `memoize` with bounded `readBody`. Native cloning after an uncached read is checked as a separate difference.
- Hono's `parseBody()` accepts a non-form request and returns an empty object. Utils `parseForm()` rejects its media
  type before reading. The tests confirm the remaining bytes are still available; they assert the public issue code
  rather than diagnostic wording.
- Hono context methods carry status, headers and response reassignment state. The Utils response examples explicitly
  compose `mergeHeaders`, `appendHeaders` and `toHeaders` with native Responses. Empty-array deletion, sequential casing
  replacement and retained headers are application choices, not hidden defaults of `mergeHeaders`.
- Utils explicitly supplies the chosen not-found representation and registers both literal paths for the Hono non-strict
  application. Its trailing-slash redirect middleware has a different contract.

The fixture does not qualify Hono-specific context type inference, bindings, execution contexts, renderers, raw router
stash internals, every built-in middleware, proxy transport, network listeners or gateway protocols. Those are separate
capabilities. The earlier [application parity corpus](../http-parity/README.md) also exercises compiled Utils service
and gateway ownership; this upstream corpus does not turn those owners into Hono APIs or add them to Hono's source
coverage.

No performance result follows from this correctness suite. The measured application corpus remains a separate fixture,
so adding upstream cases does not silently change an earlier timing workload. A successful source run also does not
prove behavior of an installed archive unless the installed-consumer lane executes this exact suite against its physical
package exports.
